script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for September 23. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
No two individuals are exactly alike—even identical twins differ.  This variation isn't error; it's strategy.  Differences mean some individuals will thrive no matter what conditions arise.

Evolution needs variation to work—selection can only favor what exists. Without differences, there's nothing to select. Variation is the raw material of adaptation. Low-variation populations are vulnerable.  The Irish Potato Famine killed millions because one potato variety dominated.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Difference is feature, not bug.  Variation provides the raw material for adaptation and progress.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Variation Value - What Diversity Do You Bring?.

Here's your activity: What makes you different—skills, perspectives, experiences, approaches? How do these differences add value to your groups and teams? In what contexts would your particular variation be especially valuable? Difference is strength. This helps you identify and leverage personal differentiation.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about why everyone's different can be applied to variation value - what diversity do you bring?. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
